text: Every day, you scroll through endless headlines, trying to stay informed. You just want clear, concise information about the world.
But lately, something feels off. Headlines scream with vague urgency: 'You WON'T believe what happened!' or 'This one trick…' It’s frustrating.
You might think it's just lazy writing or a desperate grab for your eyes. Surely, news should prioritize facts, not sensationalism?
The truth is, headlines compete in an attention economy. Algorithms reward clicks and engagement. A good headline is a carefully engineered curiosity gap.
The cost? You spend more time decoding hyperbolic promises than absorbing news. Trust erodes, and understanding gets diluted by the constant chase for your click.
Now, as you scroll again, you see the system. Every headline is a tiny hook, pulling you into a game for your attention. You know the rules, and you're harder to fool.
